nodes.name: C61 Prostatakarzinom
nodes.summary: Patient-5 has a diagnosis of C61 Prostatakarzinom (ICD-10 C61, stage cT2b cN0 cM0, Gleason 3+4=7, ISUP 2) with a history of radical prostatectomy (RPE) and biochemical recurrence undergoing salvage therapy, initially showing rising PSA levels before receiving salvage radiotherapy of the prostatic bed (66 Gy) in January 2029. Arzt-1 showed a declining and stable PSA-Verlauf with total PSA decreasing from 0,9 ng/ml in January 2029 to 0,3 ng/ml in April 2029, and maintaining at <0,1 ng/ml from August 2029 through December 16, 2030. nodes.name: Patient-5
nodes.summary:
Patient-5, born September 22, 1970 (case number URO-2026-0005), has a clinical diagnosis of C61 Prostatakarzinom with an initial PSA level of 13.4 ng/ml, an ECOG performance status ranging from 0 to 2, and TNM staging cT2b cN0 cM0. Following a radical prostatectomy (RARP) performed by Dr. med. Arzt-1 on January 22, 2027, the pathology confirmed a pT2c R0 adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 3+4=7 (ISUP 2). Subsequent follow-ups showed a stable PSA of <0,1 ng/ml through March 2028. By August 2028, the PSA rose to 0.2 ng/ml with an ansteigend trend and clinical/biochemical progression. By December 2028, the PSA increased to 0.9 ng/ml, prompting an interdisciplinary tumor conference on January 2, 2029, which recommended Salvage Radiotherapy Plus Adt. On January 4, 2029, a PSMA-PET/CT revealed focal hypermetabolism in the prostatic bed with no distant metastasis.
